1. Open the **Plugins** page in the DSH instance you want to control.

sing the page's package installation control:

3. After installation, enable DSHM on the Plugins page and open **Settings → DSHM**.
When upgrading

from 0.1.3 or earlier, use **Quit DeepSeek Harness** from the
app menu on macOS or exit DSH from its

tray menu on Windows, then reopen it
once. Closing only the window can leave the old bridge running

, even while
Plugins shows the newly installed version. Keep the bridge data: your paired
devices re
tain their access. Subsequent disable/re-enable needs no restart.

Use DSH's plugin manager rather than editing its profile files or copying files
into the installed a

pplication. The plugin is installed into the selected DSH
profile; installing it into one profile do
es not enable every other profile.

The DSH Market listing installs the package from npm. Catalog updates and npm
availability can appea

r at different times. You can also install by package
name through DSH's plugin manager.
## Pair your device
### Guided remote setup

Phone not on the same Wi-Fi as this computer? Use Tailscale. On the same Wi-Fi,
nothing else is need

ed. Open **Settings → DSHM → Not on the same Wi-Fi**.
The optional helper checks the official Tailsc

ale app on Windows/macOS, links
to its official installer instructions, and can open the installed a

pp on the
DSH host. Complete installation, system approvals and browser sign-in yourself.
If viewing

DSH from another computer, install Tailscale on the **DSH host**.
The plugin does not embed a VPN,

install software automatically, or change
Tailscale accounts, DNS, routes, exit nodes, firewall or p

re automatically, or change
Tailscale accounts, DNS, routes, exit nodes, firewall or proxy settings.

Install Tailscale on your iPhone/iPad, sign in to the same personal account,
and connect both ends.

For organization accounts, both devices must belong to
the same permitted tailnet; account sign-in d

oes not override access policy.
Then select **Pair for remote access** and scan the fresh QR in DSHM

. An older
LAN-only pairing does not automatically acquire the new VPN address: forget
the old compu

ter in DSHM, revoke its old device entry on the host, and pair again.
An active earlier QR is replac
ed when you explicitly create the fresh one.

The card distinguishes PC readiness from **Phone connected over Tailscale**.
Test with your phone on

cellular or a different Wi-Fi.
**Pair a device** remains available for ordinary LAN use without Tai

lscale.

## What is sent, and where

The bridge sends session messages, tool results, approvals, selected files and
declared deliverables

to your authenticated, paired device over pinned TLS.
Prompts, answers and attachments from that de

vice go back to DSH on your
computer. The bridge runs no cloud agent and has no analytics service or

relay
for session traffic. It does not read or forward DSH's provider-credential store.
DSH itself

still contacts the model providers and tools you configured, under
their own settings.

On the LAN, Bonjour announces the bridge's host identity/version and private
addresses for discovery

. Local bridge identity and pairing records stay under
`$DSH_HOME/dshm/` (`~/.dsh/dshm/` with the de

fault DSH home); private files should
never be pasted into issues. Installing a package or using a r

emote plugin
index makes DSH contact the package registry/index host.

**Optional push notifications use a separate proxy and Apple Push Notification
service (APNs).** Wit

hout a configured `pushProxyUrl`, the bridge makes no push
network requests and does not advertise p

ush support. Configuring a URL enables
periodic health checks; push support is advertised only while

the proxy is
reachable and the bridge's session observer is working. This package includes the brid

ge sender; the proxy and app are separate. iOS push registration,
the Notification Service Extension

and real locked-phone delivery remain
separate work; they have not been verified by the local backe

locked-phone delivery remain
separate work; they have not been verified by the local backend tests.

For push registration, the app sends its APNs device token and sandbox/production
environment to the

selected HTTPS proxy. The proxy stores that routing mapping
and encrypts its authentication secret

under a separate wrapping key. The app
shares the returned registration and a separate notification-

content key with
the paired bridge over DMP. The bridge stores these keys and preferences in its
pri

vate `$DSH_HOME/dshm/push.json` file (mode 0600). The APNs provider key stays
only in the proxy's se
cret configuration; it is never supplied to the bridge.
